extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemakers, administrative law attorneys, and environmental policy advocates submitting or evaluating notice-and-comment filings
extracted.subtask_description: A detailed coalition legal comment arguing that EPA's proposed reconsideration/repeal of the Endangerment Finding violates statutory and judicial requirements (Clean Air Act, case law) by failing to cite and weigh National Academies work, by omitting needed docket materials, and by neglecting to analyze reliance interests and sectoral impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement re: National Academy findings (42 U.S.C. §7607(d)(3)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal must “set forth or summarize and provide a reference to any pertinent findings, recommendations, and comments by … the National Academy of Sciences, and, if the proposal differs in any important respect from any of these recommendations, an explanation of the reasons for such differences.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All data, information, and documents referred to in this paragraph on which the proposed rule relies shall be included in the docket on the date of publication of the proposed rule. If EPA wishes to reassess or reject NAS/NRC findings that underlie past agency determinations, it must withdraw and reissue a proposal that complies with this statutory requirement so the public can assess EPA’s reasons for departure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing and final-rule procedural requirements (42 U.S.C. §7607(d)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: For final rules: (A) the promulgated rule must be accompanied by a statement of basis and purpose and an explanation of reasons for any major changes from the proposed rule; (B) a response to each of the significant comments, criticisms, and new data submitted; (C) the promulgated rule may not be based (in part or whole) on any information or data which has not been placed in the docket as of the date of such promulgation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must place in the docket all information on which it relies at the time of proposal and must respond to significant comments in the final rule; failing to do so violates the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to cite and give substantial weight to NAS/NRC reviews and relevant scientific assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must cite, reference, and account for pertinent National Academies reviews (e.g., the NAS review of draft NCA5 and the NAS 2025 consensus study) when those reviews bear on the proposal to reconsider or rescind the Endangerment Finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NAS review and consensus reports are central to the scientific basis for the 2009 Finding; EPA’s failure to even cite these reviews constitutes noncompliance with 42 U.S.C. §7607(d)(3)(C) and undermines the public’s ability to evaluate departures from NAS conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to incorporate and rely on best available science (weight multiple lines of evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency decisionmaking must incorporate the best-available scientific evidence: consider multiple sources of evidence, weigh evidence by type (observational evidence weighed most heavily), and give substantial weight to independent, peer-reviewed lines of evidence and consensus findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NAS report’s methodology (considering >600 peer-reviewed articles, privileging independent lines of evidence and observational data) is the sort of scientific standard EPA must consider and explain any divergence from; ignoring such methodologies or consensus findings risks an arbitrary decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reversing prior policy, provide a more detailed justification (Fox/Encino standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency action represents a reversal in prior policy, the agency must “provide a more detailed justification than what would suffice for a new policy created on a blank slate” when its new policy rests upon factual findings that contradict those underlying the prior policy or when the prior policy engendered serious reliance interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities include Fox (556 U.S. at 515), Encino Motorcars, and related D.C. Circuit precedent; the required justification must address contradicted factual determinations and reliance interests with specific, reasoned explanation rather than generalized assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must assess, determine significance of, and weigh reliance interests (Regents standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must assess whether reliance interests exist, determine whether they are significant, and weigh any such interests against competing policy concerns; interested parties need not have legally cognizable reliance interests for the agency to consider them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A policy must have been in place sufficiently long for legitimate reliance interests to develop. EPA must meaningfully evaluate reliance interests rather than make conclusory statements that such interests do not justify retaining past standards (citing Department of Homeland Security v. Regents of the University of California and Vermont Yankee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disregard prior factual determinations or rely on unexplained inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: In reversing course the agency may not “simply disregard” prior contrary factual determinations or rest its decision on unexplained inconsistencies and generalized conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities cited include Air All. Houston v. EPA and National Cable & Telecomm. Ass’n v. Brand X; the agency must provide a reasoned explanation for disregarding facts and circumstances that underlay the prior policy (Fox).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful analysis of sectoral and consumer reliance impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must analyze the specific sectoral impacts of the proposed action — e.g., effects on tourism and recreation, real estate, agriculture and fisheries, forests, insurance and reinsurance, hazardous chemicals — as well as consumer impacts (increased product, transportation, and health care costs; higher utility expenditures; employment/earnings effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA’s cursory treatment (discussing avoided compliance costs alone) is inadequate. The agency should assess sector-specific reliance interests, labor-market benefits of regulation, consumer preferences, and distributional consequences rather than only noting industry compliance costs in the aggregate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of global political, trade, and technology-diffusion reliance interests
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must consider how domestic regulatory reversals affect global political consequences, international climate leadership, technology diffusion, regulatory influence abroad, and global trade/market signaling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence that U.S. domestic policy influences foreign regulation and technology adoption (e.g., catalytic converters example) means EPA must account for these reliance interests and cannot dismiss the international implications of rescinding U.S. greenhouse-gas vehicle standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of national security implications as a reliance interest
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must analyze how greenhouse-gas deregulation implicates national security (e.g., exacerbation of geopolitical tensions, climate-related displacement, resource scarcity, and erosion of state legitimacy) as part of weighing reliance interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National security impacts are relevant reliance interests under the arbitrary-and-capricious/reversal jurisprudence and warrant meaningful consideration in the administrative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must identify and justify proposed transitional regulatory tools (no conclusory claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: If EPA claims it possesses “adequate regulatory tools to address transitional compliance concerns,” the agency must identify those tools and explain how they will address specific reliance and transition issues rather than making conclusory assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A conclusory statement that reliance interests “would not justify retaining the GHG emission standards” without describing the tools or analysis is inadequate under judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary-and-capricious constraint on reversals that run counter to evidentiary record (State Farm)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency action that ‘runs[] counter to the evidence before the agency’ is arbitrary and capricious; reversals of prior findings must be supported by reasoned analysis and record evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Ass’n v. State Farm and related standards: where the NAS and the scientific record strongly support the 2009 Finding, a proposal that contradicts that evidence must squarely confront and justify departures from the record.
